scheme_name: One Act Play competition at High School, Higher Secondary School and College level (Konkani, Marathi & English)
description:
The One Act Play competition is an initiative launched by the Government of India to promote cultural activities among students at the high school, higher secondary school, and college levels. 

This scheme specifically targets students who are engaged in the performing arts, particularly in the languages of Konkani, Marathi, and English. 

The competition aims to provide a platform for students to showcase their theatrical talents and creativity. 

The initiative was launched in the year 2015 under the aegis of the Directorate of Art and Culture, Government of Goa. 

The primary objective of the One Act Play competition is to encourage students to engage in drama and performing arts. 

The competition seeks to foster creativity and artistic expression among young individuals. 

It also aims to enhance the appreciation of literature and drama in regional languages. 

The competition is designed to promote teamwork and collaboration among students. 

By participating in this event, students can develop their communication skills and confidence. 

The One Act Play competition is held annually, with specific dates announced by the Directorate of Art and Culture. 

The competition is open to students from high schools, higher secondary schools, and colleges across Goa. 

The eligibility criteria for participation include being a registered student of the respective educational institution. 

Students must be enrolled in classes 9 to 12 for high school and higher secondary school levels. 

For college-level participants, students must be enrolled in any undergraduate program. 

There are no specific income criteria for participation in the competition. 

However, students must have a keen interest in drama and performing arts. 

The application process for the One Act Play competition involves several steps. 

Interested participants must first obtain the application form from their respective educational institutions. 

The application form can also be downloaded from the official website of the Directorate of Art and Culture. 

Once the form is completed, it must be submitted to the designated authority at the school or college. 

Each participating institution is required to submit a list of participants along with their respective plays. 

The plays must be original works or adaptations of existing works. 

The duration of each performance is typically limited to 30 minutes. 

The competition is judged by a panel of experts in the field of drama and performing arts. 

Judging criteria include originality, creativity, acting skills, and overall presentation. 

Awards and recognition are given to the top-performing teams and individuals. 

The first prize for the best performance is usually accompanied by a cash award of INR 10,000. 

The second prize typically amounts to INR 7,000. 

The third prize is often INR 5,000. 

Additionally, certificates of participation are awarded to all participants. 

The competition not only promotes artistic expression but also encourages cultural exchange among students. 

It serves as a platform for students to learn about various theatrical styles and techniques. 

The Directorate of Art and Culture also organizes workshops and training sessions leading up to the competition. 

These workshops are aimed at enhancing the skills of participants in acting, direction, and stage management. 

The competition is usually held in the month of December each year. 

The exact dates for the competition are announced in advance through official notifications. 

Participating institutions are encouraged to conduct preliminary rounds to select the best teams. 

This ensures that only the most talented performers represent their schools or colleges. 

The One Act Play competition has seen increasing participation over the years. 

In the inaugural year, around 30 institutions participated. 

By 2022, the number of participating institutions had increased to over 50. 

The competition has also gained recognition for promoting regional languages like Konkani and Marathi. 

Students are encouraged to perform in their native languages to preserve and promote cultural heritage. 

The Directorate of Art and Culture provides all necessary support and resources for the competition. 

This includes arranging venues, technical support, and promotional materials. 

The competition is also promoted through social media and local newspapers to reach a wider audience. 

The event culminates in a grand finale where the best performances are showcased. 

This finale is usually attended by dignitaries from the field of arts and culture. 

It provides an opportunity for students to network with professionals in the industry. 

The One Act Play competition not only nurtures talent but also instills a sense of discipline and dedication among students. 

Students learn the importance of teamwork and collaboration through the rehearsal process. 

The competition also encourages students to explore various themes and social issues through their performances. 

In recent years, there has been a focus on incorporating contemporary issues into the plays. 

This has led to a diverse range of performances that resonate with the audience. 

The One Act Play competition is a significant cultural event in Goa's educational calendar. 

It has become a platform for young artists to express their views and creativity. 

The initiative aligns with the government's broader goals of promoting arts and culture in education. 

Overall, the One Act Play competition serves as an important catalyst for cultural development among youth in India. 

It fosters a love for the performing arts and encourages students to pursue their passions. 

The competition continues to evolve, adapting to the changing interests and talents of students. 

The Directorate of Art and Culture remains committed to supporting and enhancing this initiative for future generations. 

Through this competition, the government aims to create a vibrant cultural landscape in educational institutions. 

The One Act Play competition is a testament to the importance of arts in education and community engagement.
